titulo: Page live and the same project on a VPS
lead: Saving, sending, and putting it live are three steps and three decisions. With an SSH key and gh, you send the project to GitHub, publish the page at an address that opens on your phone, and take the same folder to a VPS, where the agent works even when your computer is off.
objetivo: connect the terminal to GitHub with an SSH key, publish the page on GitHub Pages, and clone the project on a VPS.
hero_alt: Laptop with the terminal open and a phone beside it showing a published page; servers in the background.

aprende.t: Create the SSH key and hand over only the public one
Create the repository, publish on Pages, and the push routine
Check destination, status, versions, and secrets before sending
Log in to the VPS, clone the project, and bring in what changed

secoes.sub: GitHub is the bridge between your computer, the page, and the VPS.

nos.detalhe: The private key never leaves here. The commit saves the version only on your computer; nothing goes to the internet until you decide to send it.
The push sends the versions. Public repository: anyone can see it (and it's what the free page requires). Private: only you and the people you invite. You choose when you create it.
Putting it online is one extra step. Once Pages is on, every push updates the page within a few minutes, at an address that opens on your phone.

nos.sub: A rented computer, on all the time
nos.detalhe: A rented room: the provider hands over the machine; users, updates, and programs are up to you. You log in through ssh, move around with Linux names, and bring the project over from GitHub.

secoes.volta: Changed on the computer → push → git pull on the VPS
secoes.legenda: The public key (.pub) is the padlock: it goes to GitHub and to the VPS. The private one is the key on your keyring: it stays with you.

rolagem_fim.texto: The commit stays on your computer, the push takes it to GitHub, and Pages puts it online. The VPS gets the same version with git pull. Each step is your decision, with its own check.

texto: ssh-keygen already comes with Windows 10 and 11. It asks three questions: where to save, and an extra password, twice. Enter on all three is fine for practice.
Two files end up in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh: id_ed25519 (private, never leaves there) and id_ed25519.pub (public).

exemplo.texto: You already have a key: answer n and use the one you have.

texto: Answer: GitHub.com → SSH → choose id_ed25519.pub → Login with a web browser. Copy the code, paste it in the browser, and authorize.
ssh -T git@github.com tests the key; the first time, answer yes.
Destination: git remote -v shows where it goes. Status: git status is clean. Versions: git log --oneline shows what would go. Secrets: no .env in the list.
Once sent, the content belongs to whoever has access to the destination.

exemplo.texto: Anyone can see it. No personal drafts and no keys.

texto: ssh root@IP-DA-VPS opens the VPS terminal in your window. The start of the line changes and ends in # or $: always check which machine you are on before each command.
There: ls instead of dir, pwd instead of cd on its own, and capital letters matter.

exemplo.texto: Did you change how you log in? Test it in a new window before closing the one that works.

secoes.sub: Replace Seu Nome, seu@email.com, SEU-USUARIO and IP-DA-VPS with your own.

blocos.rot: cmd · who you are in Git (for all projects)
blocos.conteudo:
git config --global user.name "Seu Nome"
git config --global user.email "seu@email.com"
git config --global --list

blocos.rot: cmd · connect gh to your account
cmd · create the repository and push
blocos.conteudo:
cd %USERPROFILE%\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente
git status
git branch -M main
gh repo create meu-primeiro-agente --public --source=. --push

git status
git add .
git commit -m "o que mudou"
git push

blocos.rot: VPS (Linux) · log in, clone and update
blocos.conteudo:
ssh root@IP-DA-VPS
mkdir -p ~/projetos
cd ~/projetos
apt update && apt install -y git
git clone https://github.com/SEU-USUARIO/meu-primeiro-agente.git
cd meu-primeiro-agente
ls
git pull
exit

blocos.rot: VPS (Linux) · the agent on the server

abas.html:
C:\Users\ana> ssh -T git@github.com
Hi ana-exemplo! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.
C:\Users\ana\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente> gh repo create meu-primeiro-agente --public --source=. --push
✓ Created repository ana-exemplo/meu-primeiro-agente on GitHub

A few minutes after you turn on Pages, the page opens at https://ana-exemplo.github.io/meu-primeiro-agente/.

• "nothing to commit": the folder is empty or already saved. Check with dir and git log --oneline.
  • "Name already exists": a repository with that name already exists in your account. Pick another one.
  • Push rejected with "fetch first": the repository changed somewhere else. Run git pull and then git push.
  • "No such file or directory" on the VPS: check capital letters and use Tab to autocomplete.

abas.rot: Which file do you hand over?
abas.html: Someone asked for your key "to set up access": only the id_ed25519.pub. The id_ed25519, without .pub, never leaves your computer.

secoes.titulo: Rehearse: the project on the VPS
secoes.sub: Same navigation, different names. Look at the start of the line.

missoes.pede: Log in to the VPS as root (the example IP is 203.0.113.10).
missoes.explica: The start of the line changed: now the VPS's Linux is answering. Same window, different machine.

missoes.pede: Ask where you are (on Linux it's pwd).
missoes.explica: pwd does the job of the bare cd in cmd.
The -p creates it and doesn't complain if it already exists. The ~ is the home folder, like %USERPROFILE%.

missoes.pede: Bring the project over from GitHub (user ana-exemplo).
missoes.explica: The clone brings the folder and its whole history. Cloning doesn't run anything.

missoes.pede: Go into the folder and list its contents (two commands: cd first).
List what came over (on Linux it's ls).
missoes.explica: The same files from your Windows machine. The .env didn't come, because it never went to GitHub.

missoes.pede: You changed something on Windows and pushed. Bring the change over.
missoes.explica: GitHub is the bridge: the new version reached the VPS.
Back on your computer: the start of the line is C:\Users\ana again.

secoes.fim: Project moved to the VPS and updated. In real life, the agent runs in there with the same AGENTS.md.
secoes.legenda: Simulation: the IP, user and codes are examples (203.0.113.10 is an address reserved for documentation).

secoes.sub: The live page is required; the VPS, once you have one.

exercicios.texto: Create the SSH key, run gh auth login choosing SSH, and test with ssh -T git@github.com.
exercicios.pronto: the response starts with "Hi" followed by your GitHub username.

exercicios.texto: Do the four-point check, create the public repository, turn on Pages, then change something and run the add, commit and push routine.
exercicios.pronto: the page opens on your phone at https://SEU-USUARIO.github.io/meu-primeiro-agente/ and the change shows up after the push.

exercicios.titulo: E17 · The same project on the VPS
exercicios.texto: On an Ubuntu VPS set up with your public key, log in with ssh, clone the project, change something on Windows, push, and bring it over with git pull.
exercicios.pronto: ls on the VPS shows the files and git pull brought the change made on Windows.

secoes.titulo: The whole step, command by command
secoes.sub: From the empty terminal on Windows to the site on GitHub Pages and the project running on the VPS.
Pick the start date and how much time you have per week. The plan spreads the course's 17 exercises across it.

txt.travou: ## What got stuck and the rule I created

itens.texto: Before any command, look at the path before the >. The wrong folder looks like an AI failure.
One subject per folder, a README for people, and an AGENTS.md with rules you can check.
Keep secrets in .env and out of Git; commit before a big change; restore when you don't like it.
Saving, sending, and putting online are three steps. The agent does the work; you check and approve.

secoes.sub: About this lesson and the whole step.

perguntas.p: Someone asked for your SSH key to "set up access." Which file can you hand over?
perguntas.explica: The .pub is the padlock: it can go to GitHub, to the VPS, or to anyone who needs to grant you access. The private key never leaves your computer.

perguntas.p: You ran git commit. Is the version on GitHub yet?
opcoes: No: a commit saves on your computer; git push is what sends it.
Only if the repository is public.
perguntas.explica: Saving, sending, and putting online are three separate steps: commit, push, and Pages.

perguntas.p: Before a push to a public repository, what do you check?
opcoes: The destination, the state of the folder, the versions that would go, and no secrets.
Only whether the page looks nice.
perguntas.explica: Four points: git remote -v, git status, git log --oneline, and no .env or key. If it's public, anyone can see it.

perguntas.p: On the VPS, the line starts with root@minha-vps:~#. Where are you?
opcoes: On the VPS, in root's home folder.
perguntas.explica: The start of the line tells you which machine you're on. ~ is the home folder; on Windows the line would start with C:\Users\.
